title: Grilled Tofu Veggie Tacos
subtitle: with basil pesto
menu_blurb: Soft tortillas filled with marinated grilled tofu, eggplant, mushrooms and spinach, layered with a bright, dairy-free basil pesto.
intro: A super yummy take on soft tacos with a delicious pesto. My favorite part is the eggplant. I can’t wait to see what you like best!
origin: Tacos began in pre-Columbian Mexico, where Indigenous peoples, including the Aztecs, used flat corn tortillas as edible spoons for fish, beans, and chiles. The word taco comes from the Nahuatl tlahco, meaning “half” or “in the middle.” Pesto comes from Genoa in northern Italy and dates to the 16th century. Its name comes from the Italian pestare, “to pound,” and its true ancestor is the ancient Roman moretum, a pounded paste of herbs, garlic, and cheese.

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Eggplant, mushrooms, spinach, tofu, and red onion

items.name: Large eggplant, sliced ¼ inch thick
Fresh basil, packed, large stems removed

steps.title: Marinate the tofu
instructions: Slice the tofu and marinate it while you prepare the vegetables.

steps.title: Grill the vegetables and tofu
instructions: Slice the eggplant about ¼ inch thick, slice the mushrooms and red onion, and roughly chop the spinach.
Spray with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and grill or griddle the vegetables in batches.
Do the same with the tofu, then set everything aside.

steps.title: Make the pesto
instructions: Blend all of the pesto ingredients until smooth.
Taste and adjust the salt or acidity.

steps.title: Assemble
instructions: Add the tofu, then layer in the vegetables and sliced avocado.
Fold over and toast on a griddle sprayed with olive oil, turning once.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add a spicy taco seasoning to the tofu.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Swap the eggplant for zucchini, and use mini or large tortillas.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keeps for a couple of days in the fridge and makes a great appetizer. The pesto doubles as a salad dressing, a dip, or a mayonnaise replacement.

notebook.question: What is tofu, and is it good for you?
answer: Tofu is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein made from curdled soy milk pressed into blocks. It is a complete protein with all nine essential amino acids, and it is high in iron and calcium. It supports heart health, may reduce the risk of certain cancers, and aids weight management.
Its nutrition varies with firmness. Firmer varieties hold less water, so they carry more protein, fat, and calories per serving.

table.label: Extra firm
table.text: 15 to 17 g protein and about 145 calories

table.label: Firm
table.text: 8 to 10 g protein and 70 to 80 calories

table.label: Silken or soft
table.text: About 4 to 7 g protein and 40 to 62 calories

benefits.label: Heart health
benefits.text: Cholesterol-free and low in saturated fat, tofu may help reduce LDL cholesterol. Studies show eating at least one serving a week may lower heart disease risk by 18%.

benefits.label: Nutrient-rich
benefits.text: A good source of iron, manganese, selenium, phosphorus, and calcium, especially when made with calcium sulfate.

benefits.label: Bone health
benefits.text: Its high calcium and magnesium content helps prevent osteoporosis.

notebook.question: What is nutritional yeast, and is it good for you?
answer: Nutritional yeast is a deactivated yeast from the same species used to bake bread and brew beer. The yeast cells are inactive, so it won’t make bread rise or ferment anything.
It is exceptionally good for you, with plant protein, fiber, and B vitamins in very few calories, which makes it a favorite in vegan and plant-based kitchens.
